summary.headline: Steelcast Q1 FY27 revenue rose 17% to INR124.82 crores and PAT 19.26% to INR23.71 crores; management guides 25-30% FY27 volume growth.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR124.82 crores, up 17% YoY, with EBITDA of INR35.24 crores (28.23% margin vs 28.14%) and PAT of INR23.71 crores (19% margin vs 18.64%). Management said input-cost increases will be passed through via sales price variation formulas, with the bulk of the price correction effective 1 July. Capacity utilisation was 66% in April-June, and a greenfield foundry of 8,500 tonnes (about INR120 crores over two years) was approved, targeted for commissioning by 31 March FY28. The order book stood at INR140 crores, roughly 3-4 months of forward booking.

financial_highlights.change: Export share 60% by tonnage (management also cited 62% by value)
Not quantified vs last year; management said it is higher

segments.name: Sector mix (sales, current year guidance)
segments.commentary: Mining about 27%, earthmoving about 43%, construction about 15%, defense about 1%, with the remainder across other sectors. Ten years ago mining was about 84% of sales, earthmoving near zero and construction 15-16%.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Exports have historically run at 45-50% of sales; FY27 guided at about 49-50% exports, and the next year at 47% exports and 53% domestic. Sales now go to about 16 countries; the US and Germany together are about 70% of exports.

segments.name: Ground engaging tools (GET)
segments.commentary: Under 1% of revenue today, with FY26 at about 1%; guided to about 3.5% of sales in FY27 and 4.5-5% by FY29 as new parts move into serial supply.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth guided at about 25% over FY26; in Q&A the chairman said 30% volume growth is a distinct possibility, and FY27 volume was implied at about 18,000 tons at 63% utilisation.
Long-term growth target of about 20% CAGR over the coming years.
Sequential quarter-on-quarter top-line improvement expected for several quarters.
EBITDA margin guided to stay in range; in Q&A the chairman said a 150-200 bps rise to 28.5-29% for FY27 is theoretically achievable and is the aim. FY27 margin was about 27%.
Price correction for input costs (raw materials and natural gas) effective 1 July, passed through under the sales price variation formula with a one-quarter lag.
Capacity utilisation target of 63% for FY27 and 90% by FY29 on existing capacity; management said above 90% is not advisable.
New facility revenue potential at peak about INR300 crores; commissioning target 31 March FY28.
Two renewable power projects (2.4 MW wind-solar hybrid and 1.4 MW solar) expected to be commissioned before 31 December 2026.
capex_capacity: Greenfield foundry of 8,500 tonnes approved by the Board, steel castings from 5 kg to 1,000 kg, planned investment about INR120 crores over two years, with an internal commissioning target of 31 March FY28.
Land of about 100,000 sq m provided by the Gujarat government; the new site is 12 km from the existing facility.
Existing capacity is about 29,000 tonnes; FY27 utilisation target is 63% and 90% by FY29.
Plan to start recruiting around mid-year for FY28 readiness; staff currently adequate for FY27 targets.
Considering shifting some manufacturing fuel from natural gas to electricity over 2-3 years; natural gas is about 50-55% more expensive than at end-February prices.
demand_pricing: Pricing is pass-through under a sales price variation formula with customers; the chairman said all major raw material increases will be recovered, but declined to give a percentage range.
Over 100 new parts developed in the last 18-24 months; about 20% of revenue expected from new parts over the next 2-3 years, with 80% from existing parts.
Management said US railroad work has been deprioritised in favour of better-priced industrial markets, and defense is a low priority because pricing is better elsewhere.
Rupee movements are shared with customers, not hedged.
Management says all 9 end-user sectors are seeing demand increases, with automobile growing 10-15%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the input-cost increase will be passed to customers, and how much is done so far?
qa_highlights.answer: Only a minimal correction took effect 1 April; most comes from 1 July. All major raw materials are in the formula, so the chairman said all increases will be passed on, without quantifying a range.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 25% growth mean volume or volume plus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth of 25%, with price increases on top; the chairman later said 30% volume growth is a distinct possibility.

qa_highlights.question: Will utilisation reach 100% by FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Target is 90% by FY29 on existing capacity, and new capacity starts adding volume afterwards.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement and what is the new facility's peak revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly scale and operating leverage, with minimal price increase so far. Peak revenue potential from the new facility is about INR300 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company considering a rights issue or bonus issue, and is it focusing on defense?
qa_highlights.answer: Company has about INR120 crores of reserves and will fund the capex from internal accruals; a rights issue is not needed because it would dilute EPS. A bonus issue will be taken to the next Board meeting. Defense is deprioritised because it is a single-customer, higher-risk business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the segment split and how has it changed over 10 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Mining, earthmoving and construction together are about 70% of sales. Mining fell from about 84% to about 54% over 10 years, and earthmoving rose from near zero to about 36%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk that exports are understated because of Tier 2 supply to OEMs?
qa_highlights.answer: The chairman said 98-99% of sales are direct Tier 1 supply to OEMs, and OEMs may export part of what they buy, so total export share may be a little higher.

risks_watch: Realisation of the 1 July price correction, which management says follows a one-quarter lag and has not been quantified.
Inventory build (WIP) during the ramp-up; management described it as a 1-2 month timing effect, to be watched in Q2.
Natural gas and energy cost volatility, with gas about 50-55% higher than end-February prices.
Concentration: the US and Germany account for about 70% of exports, and mining, earthmoving and construction for about 70% of sales.
Tracking of the 25-30% volume guidance and the INR140 crores order book against actual quarterly top line.
Israel defense component trials, which management expects to hear on in coming months.
Recruitment plan from mid-year for FY28 capacity.
key_quotes: And all the major raw materials are part of the formula, and we will be able to pass on everything, all increases.
So, quarter-on-quarter, you will see improved sales.
Yes, theoretically, that should happen, and this is what we are going to strive to achieve.
Yes, you are right. I did say 25%, I should have said 30% because indications from most of our customers are very strong.
summary.management_tone: Confident and growth-oriented on demand, order book and capacity plans, with a constructive tone on pricing pass-through. Cautious or evasive on specifics: he declined to give a price-increase percentage range, said the margin target was "theoretically" achievable, and corrected his own 25% volume guidance to 30% as a distinct possibility.

adds.what: 8,500 tonne greenfield steel castings foundry (5 kg to 1,000 kg castings) in Gujarat
2.4 MW wind-solar hybrid and 1.4 MW solar renewable power projects (power, not production capacity)

growth.why: Management guides ~25% FY27 volume growth (possibly 30%) against a 48% FY26 utilisation and 66% Q1 utilisation, backed by a INR140 crore order book (~3-4 months) and pass-through pricing, while the 8,500 t greenfield foundry (INR120 crore) targets commissioning by 31 March FY28, so it adds no FY27 volume.
